Every error is a fixed string through falhar() (lines 48-52), and psql stderr is never echoed (lines 141-145). backup_private.py strips the secret env vars (lines 53-55). It maps stderr to fixed categories (lines 72-85) and replaces tracebacks with a generic message (lines 225-228); its log line has aggregates only (lines 212-213). check_deploy.mjs sends the bypass only as a header, and only to allowlisted hosts (lines 29-44, 62-63). Step summaries carry only the semgrep manifest, the graft map and the git diff of versioned baseline JSON (atualizar-baseline.yml:117-125), with no secret material. checks.invariant: No weak randomness, crypto-primitive misuse, timing-sensitive secret comparison or fail-open crypto path.

hardening: .gitignore (lines 9-11) ignores only .env and .env.*. Add *.pem, *.key, *.p12, credentials*.json, service-account*.json, *.age, divat-backup*/ and .claude/settings.local.json so that an operator's local key file, a downloaded encrypted backup artifact, or Claude Code local permission rules (which can embed command lines carrying credentials) cannot be committed by accident. Verified uncovered by git check-ignore (agents/h23-secrets-obvious/artifacts/check-01.out).

scripts/lib/audit-database.mjs:37 accepts sslmode=require, which does not verify the server certificate. Without require_auth=scram-sha-256, libpq also honors a cleartext-password request from an impostor server. An on-path attacker between the runner and Supabase could therefore obtain the divat_auditor_ci password, which grants read-only metadata/audit diagnostics. The sibling backup_private.py:59,153 already uses verify-full with sslrootcert=system. This is owner-pending per docs/seguranca.md:148-152. Fix: accept only verify-full and set PGREQUIREAUTH=scram-sha-256 in the child env.

scripts/restore_rest.mjs:234 prints the full PostgREST INSERT error body, which can quote row values from the backup, and :206 echoes the JSON.parse message of a malformed legacy key payload. This is a local operator tool, so there is no CI exposure. Prefer status plus code only.

The deleted project's anon JWT (ref lwzsxuaqqeoamukduhev, role=anon) remains in reachable history, and .codex/config.toml:2 still points an MCP server at that ref. The project is reported deleted, so the authority is nil; remove the stale config entry for hygiene.

uncovered.reason: deploy-smoke.yml:41 places the bypass secret in job env, and :62 checks out the default GITHUB_SHA. For deployment_status events that is the deployed commit, so the workflow definition and code come from whatever commit the Vercel app deployed. That can include fork or PR-head commits if Vercel fork protection or repo visibility allows it. Whether non-writer code can run with the secret depends on GitHub's deployment_status semantics and Vercel Git fork-protection settings. This is a CI trust-boundary question outside secret-hygiene/obvious-checklist scope and needs its own owner if no CI-secrets unit covers it.
